subject: Helios - follow-up: targeted model-quality tests & hyperscaler comparison
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Cole <evan.cole@helios.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.s@helios.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Recap + proposed evaluation scope (post-demo)

Evan / Priya — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our side and a concrete proposal for the next 2 weeks so we can get apples-to-apples data vs the hyperscalers: 

Key requirements we captured
- Sub-200ms token tail latency for interactive agents at 2 concurrent users (99th pctl target)
- Hallucination rate <= 1.5% on your internal factual dataset (we'll use your supplied gold corpus)
- Support for VPC deploy or private routing for sensitive queries

What Redwood proposes as a first evaluation bundle
1) Sanity run (48h): 1M tokens across 3 prompt families (FAQ, multi-hop reasoning, entity-centric extraction) against: Redwood-pinned model, AWS Bedrock equivalent, GCP Vertex equivalent
2) Model-quality tests: 300 prompt samples with structured rubric (factuality / attribution / fluency) and automated hallucination detector + human spot checks
3) Perf/cost matrix: identical input distribution, measure latency, tokens/sec, and TCO estimate normalized to your workload

Attached: model_eval_prompts.md (prompt families + scoring notes), and a short rubric we'll use to label hallucinations. Marissa will follow up with the detailed test matrix and a short sanity-run CSV you can review.

Asks from Helios to proceed
- Confirm dataset transfer method (S3 link or secure Share?) and whether we can cache a read-only copy in our private test VPC
- Provide an APi/ingest key or test account for Bedrock/Vertex so we can run the exact same evaluation harness (if you prefer, we can run calls from your account with your creds)
- Any additional regulatory constraints (PII masking rules, retention windows) we should honor during test logging

Proposed timeline
- Confirm above items by Fri 6/12 -> kickoff lightweight sanity run week of 6/15 -> full comparative run w/ annotations by 6/22

Thanks — I’ll coordinate a 30m touchpoint next week once we have the transfer and keys.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198

[attachment: model_eval_prompts.md (text/markdown)]

From: Evan Cole <evan.cole@helios.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.s@helios.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Recap + proposed evaluation scope (post-demo)

Appreciate the clear recap, Neha — this aligns with what we need. A couple of clarifications before we hand over datasets and creds:

- Dataset: we'll provide an S3 presigned bucket (read-only). Size: ~12k documents, ~750k tokens for the initial corpus. Is that sufficient for the sanity run?
- Bedrock/GCP creds: we'd prefer Redwood to run using our tenant creds so the cost figures reflect our org. I'll coordinate with infra to share short-lived keys.
- Privacy: we cannot export raw logs outside of our VPC. Would you be able to run the Bedrock runs from within our account (you referenced this option) and send anonymized metrics only?

Also: Can you include a short SOC 2 evidence pack and details on how Redwood handles KMS/HSM for Private deployments? That will be needed for procurement.

If you can accommodate the in-account run and the privacy constraints, we can sign off on the timeline and aim for the 6/15 kickoff.

—Evan
Evan Cole, Senior ML Platform Lead
Helios Analytics
evanc@helios.ai | +1 617 555 0144

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Cole <evan.cole@helios.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.s@helios.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2026 08:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Evaluation plan + initial sanity-run snapshot

Evan / Priya — looping in the proposed test plan and quick sanity snapshot. I built the matrix to minimize confounds between providers (same tokenization + prompt plumbing). Attached: eval_rubric.xlsx, initial_sanity_results.csv.

Short notes on methodology:
- Prompt families: FAQ (templated), Multi-hop (2-step reasoning), Attribution (asked-for-source). Each family: 100 samples for the full run; sanity uses 30 each.
- Scoring: automated factuality score (string-match + NER-based fact alignment) + two human raters for disagreements > 15%
- Latency measurement: client-side 99th pctl (reported) and server-side avg token time (if provider exposes). We'll capture both.

Initial sanity snapshot (sanity run, 90 samples):
Provider, Avg latency (ms), 99p latency (ms), Hallucination rate (%)
Redwood (opt-q4), 85, 210, 1.1
AWS Bedrock (x-variant), 120, 340, 1.9
GCP Vertex (y-variant), 110, 300, 2.3

Notes: these are from a quick lab environment with small batch sizes — not the 48h controlled run. Treat as directional. We saw particularly lower hallucination on the Redwood-quantized path for the attribution prompts; we will include more human labels to validate.

Attachments:
- eval_rubric.xlsx (scoring matrices & rater instructions)
- initial_sanity_results.csv (sample outputs + meta)

Forwarding the rubric and small result set for your review. Once we have the S3 read-only bucket and your short-lived creds, we can run within your account and provide anonymized logs and the final annotated dataset for you to keep.

—Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Cole <evan.cole@helios.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.s@helios.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2026 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluation plan + initial sanity-run snapshot

Evan — thanks for the quick thumbs-up. 

To make the hyperscaler comparison airtight, proposed controlled A/B test approach:
- We'll run the comparative harness from your AWS account (you provide short-lived keys). Redwood will deploy a dedicated test runner in your account with strict logging that only writes anonymized metrics back to our console.
- Test-matrix (attached): 1M tokens per provider, identical seed prompts, pinned model variants. We'll do two runs: 1) default quantization, 2) quantized opt path (as Marissa noted).
- Acceptance gates: if hallucination delta > 0.8% in favor of Redwood on the attribution family, we’ll prepare an expanded human review and a joint write-up to present to your stakeholders.

Can we lock a 45m sync on Mon 6/15 11:00am ET to finalize keys and the kickoff checklist? If that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short pre-kick doc (test-matrix.csv attached).

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
